query: If teams adopted the goal-management practices described by top performers, how much would achievement improve?

per_column.name: primary_lever
per_column.rationale: Captures the core practice type described, giving a strong grouping axis to compare achievement across goal-management approaches. Readings are sound (process_optimization, engagement_program), though the premium-subscription row labeled product_expansion is a mild stretch.

per_column.name: initiative_type
per_column.rationale: Provides a complementary categorization of how the goal is pursued. Somewhat overlapping with primary_lever but a distinct axis. The revenue-growth row mapped to process_redesign is weakly supported by its text.

per_column.name: goal_specificity
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to the query about goal-management practices; distinguishing quantified target vs baseline+target is a strong analytical lever. Values match the text (baseline stated 78%-90% -> baseline_and_target).

per_column.name: comparison_reference
per_column.rationale: A meaningful practice dimension (benchmarking against prior periods). Mostly well grounded; the Q4 customer-satisfaction row labeled specific_period rather than no_reference is a defensible but slightly loose reading.

per_column.name: timeframe_horizon
per_column.rationale: Time-horizon of goals is a relevant management practice axis. Values align with the text (Q4 -> within_quarter, fiscal year -> within_fiscal_year).

per_column.name: multi_initiative_complexity
per_column.rationale: Captures whether a goal bundles multiple initiatives, a plausible driver of achievement. The customer-satisfaction row (after-sales support AND personalized interactions -> True) is reasonable, though the boolean is somewhat coarse.

per_column.name: scope_of_change
per_column.rationale: Useful axis to compare achievement by breadth of change. However 'company_wide' is applied where the text is often silent on scope (cost-reduction across functions), suggesting some over-confident defaulting.

per_column.name: measurement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the existing 'metric' column, reducing added leverage. Values appear to mirror 'metric' even when it contradicts the description (satisfaction goal with metric Expense Ratio labeled expense_ratio; revenue goal labeled survey_score), propagating mismatches rather than reading the text.

per_column.name: automation_as_mechanism
per_column.rationale: A relevant practice flag given automation is a top lever, but as a near-constant boolean (452/98) it adds limited leverage. Values (all False in samples) are consistent with texts that mention no automation.

per_column.name: technology_enabler
per_column.rationale: Plausible practice dimension but overlaps conceptually with automation_as_mechanism and is skewed/bare boolean, giving modest analytical value. Sample values are well grounded.

per_column.name: feedback_loop_present
per_column.rationale: Feedback loops are a credible top-performer practice, so the flag has some value despite being a skewed boolean. Grounding is mostly sound, though the engagement-program-with-survey row marked False is arguably inconsistent.

judge.rationale: Most added columns supply genuine, distinct axes (goal_specificity, comparison_reference, timeframe_horizon, primary_lever, scope_of_change) that directly support comparing achievement across goal-management practices, which is exactly what the query needs. A cluster of skewed booleans (automation_as_mechanism, technology_enabler, feedback_loop_present) overlap and add limited leverage, and measurement_mechanism is largely redundant with the existing 'metric' column while propagating its contradictions with the descriptions. Grounding is generally solid and silent rows are handled sensibly (no_reference, not_specified), with only occasional over-confident defaults (scope company_wide) and a couple of loose mappings.
